en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape that you can clearly see from Legazpi City.
The Puerto Princesa Underground River in Palawan flows directly into the sea, making its lower half subject to ocean tides.
Taal Lake in Batangas contains Volcano Island, which itself holds a smaller body of water called the Main Crater Lake.
The Sierra Madre mountain range along the eastern coast of Luzon acts as a natural barrier against strong Pacific typhoons.
Mount Pulag in Benguet features a mossy forest where thick fog and cold temperatures cause moss to cover the trees.
Tubbataha Reef in the Sulu Sea is a massive coral atoll with colorful marine life visible just below the ocean surface.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol turn brown during the dry season because the grass covering the mounds dries up.
The white sand beaches of Boracay Island are made primarily of crushed coral and shells broken down by waves.
Lake Balinsasayao in Negros Oriental is a deep body of water formed inside the collapsed crater of a dormant volcano.
The Hinatuan Enchanted River in Surigao del Sur has exceptionally clear blue water because it originates from deep underground springs.
The towering limestone cliffs of El Nido in Palawan were formed over millions of years from ancient crushed coral reefs.
The Philippine eagle builds its massive nest high up in the tall native trees of Mount Apo National Park.
